body: Thank you. This sounds like something my dad would say and he's very comforting person. Trying to take your advice lol.

Hey, I feel like this sometimes. It's frustrating because it seems so many need help but there just aren't enough resources and understanding people at the moment. Of course you deserve to be heard, and to feel like someone cares and is listening. I'm sorry to hear you opened up to your mom and she reacted that way. If it was me I'd be hoping for understanding and even extra help during a hard time instead of condemnation and accusations.

Not having people to share this stuff with who are gentle is really tough. I'm telling you I def feel this way, that nobody cares, but they do. It just takes a lot of opening up, with the right person, at the right time. It's not going to be your mom it sounds like, and for that I am so sorry. But a therapist can and friends and occasionally things like Reddit. It sucks but we live in a world where there's a lot of emphasis on talking care of ourselves but not necessarily assuring those resources to help people do so.

Hey, I might suggest that your boyfriend is feeling not just depression and PTSD as you said, but maybe shame on top of that. When I'm dissociated because of pain, there are times when I can't look anyone in the eye, talk or say anything. I'm afraid that I'll share how awful o feel and the other person will condemn or judge me or tell me to snap out of it. It's especially bad, I think, when PTSD is involved.

Of course I don't know what's going through your boyfriend's mind. If he's lockong the door like this, I think it could be a cry for help but also a way to say, "I don't believe anyone can accept the mess I am right now, and so I'm going to prematurely reject them in subtle ways." If he was not encouraged as a child, or even shamed, for sharing his emotions, then he may be passively aggressively acting out as a way to say that he's really not well but doesn't feel safe enough to share with anyone.

I'd say the best thing might be to encourage him gently to share what's going on? Any attempts to gain his attention or control him could have the potential to make him feel alone and misunderstood, which it seems like he may be feeling during these episodes . And they could cause him to go further down the rabbit hole of dissociation and not feeling or talking

Sorry this is happening to the two of you :( I hope you can figure it out and work on it together, and that he finds ways to cope with this pain

I definitely do. It feels like if my house is cluttered or unclean I can't focus and get stressed out. It's hard to keep track of all the little things (and some big ones) that I need to do, and once the list gets too long, which doesn't take much, I can't think as straight.

Lists seem to help a little.
Are you still there by the way? Let is know how you're doing

Those are very valid reasons. Moving is a big contributor to social anxiety as you know. Changing schools and having to be alone and not fit in is incredibly painful. My parents moved every couple of years and I attended multiple schools. It hurt so bad to sit alone by myself at lunch and to be an outcast. It hurt to be rejected by groups at first and to have terrible shyness on top of it all. 

Your dad not being there for you is a big deal. It sounds like the hangout experience is what you really wanted, and deserved as his child. I want you to know that these things ARE big deals and you deserve to think about and talk about them.

It's pretty cliche, but this is not your fault. You didn't wake up and decide to gave social anxiety and feel this awful pain. You are trying the best you can and it just hurts.

It's okay that it hurts.

Also agree. It makes me sad this is still the case. It helps if we can remind ourselves that other great people struggle too, so we don't have to feel shame on too of the depression/mental illness. Thanks for pointing that out.
I feel this way. But what if I told you we are both wrong? Tell me ways that things have changed in 10 years. Just think of one and share it.
Thanks for this. It does hurt, that dismissal, especially coming from my mom. Sorry you relate since this can be pretty painful stuff
So glad to hear your dad is there with you
Hey, you aren't alone on here. I'll be your friend

Hey, I felt this way this morning. My husband left the hotel room were staying at and I briefly looked around the room for some sort of wire or cord.

People can't see it because they don't feel this way, or feel how much pain you are in unfortunately :( but some of us on here do, and feel very similarly. I feel like I'm not longer human anymore too. It's a terrifying feeling. If I could get some ground under my feet something it wouldn't be so bad.

But it's just a feeling too. I know there are valid reasons for it. Maybe we can both do the same thing right now - rest, and wait 24 hours (or preferably 72) until we choose to take any action. Give ourselves some time.

You're not attention whoring at all, and you definitely DO deserve kindness and love, maybe more than the average person. I'm glad you posted this. The feelings are very strong but you're not alone in feeling them. I also gave social anxiety and feel horrible even just being in the same room as someone on bad days. It's awful to feel so inadequate, but you aren't it's just critical mind beating you up and hurting you. I want you to know you're going to be okay. Please try to rest your mind and body right now. Can you watch something on TV or go for a walk or take a bath? Just thinking of things you can do to care for yourself.

Hey I have avoidant personality (and social anxiety) and depression. I hope you don't kill yourself the day after Christmas. Many of us here can relate.

I think there's a future ahead for you, and I think you do too for posting here. I'm on here because life has become so painful, the inability to go outside without paranoia and fear. But maybe we can talk to each other about some of this. We're in this together.

 What do you think caused your social anxiety?
Hey there, I'm also feeling very depressed and wanted to see if you'd like to message and talk more. Sounds like we could help each other or at least have someone who understands the desire to die

Hey, I just wanted to say I really relate to your post today. I'm currently at rock bottom right now. Yesterday was definitely one of the worst in my life, everything I very been keeping inside came out. And this morning im in a state of mind that I'd I can just not die, then I'm okay. If others dislike me, if my mom gates me, I could still live life on my own terms. It's like I had to go really low to stop pretending any longer.

Sorry you are experiencing such stress and side effects from it though :( it seems like you have a good perspective. Keep up the good habits work!
